# telnyx_network_routes (Data Source)

Lists network routes, with optional filters. Each item has the attributes of `telnyx_network_route`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `filter_cidr` (String) Only routes with this CIDR.
- `filter_network_id` (String) The id of the Network whose route table is returned. Required.
- `filter_next_hop_type` (String) Only routes whose next hop has this type. One of `ipsec_tunnel`, `private_wireless_gateway`, `public_internet_gateway`, `tunnel`, `virtual_cross_connect`, `wireguard_interface`, `wireguard_peer`.
- `filter_origin` (String) Only routes of this origin. One of `attachment`, `static`.
- `filter_status` (String) Only routes with this status. One of `active`, `failed`, `inactive`, `pending`.
- `max_items` (Number) Stop reading after this many items. By default every page is read.
- `sort` (String) One of `-cidr`, `-created_at`, `-status`, `cidr`, `created_at`, `status`.

### Read-Only

- `network_routes` (Attributes List) The objects, in the order the API returns them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_routes))

<a id="nestedatt--network_routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_routes`

Read-Only:

- `cidr` (String) The IPv4 CIDR the route covers.
- `created_at` (String) ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.
- `id` (String) Identifies the resource.
- `network_id` (String) The id of the Network the route belongs to.
- `next_hop` (Attributes) Where the Network sends traffic for the route's CIDR. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_routes--next_hop))
- `origin` (String) `static` for a route added with `POST /network_routes`, `attachment` for a route that another resource installed and removes.
- `record_type` (String) Identifies the type of the resource.
- `status` (String) `pending` until Telnyx installs the route on the Network, then `active`. `inactive` while a tunnel next hop has no connected process. `failed` (Preview, not reported yet) when Telnyx could not install the route.

<a id="nestedatt--network_routes--next_hop"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_routes.next_hop`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The id of the tunnel or attachment.
- `type` (String) The type of the next hop. Routes added with `POST /network_routes` use `tunnel`. Routes that attachments install carry the attachment's type.
